output.brief: Last week's 5xx rate (0.41%) is inside the normal band: the 26-week mean is 0.354% and the upper edge is 0.482%. Three earlier weeks went higher, and investigating them found nothing. The burn rate is 0.82x, well under the 2x paging threshold. Bookings and retry success didn't change, and support logged no complaints. The "new pods error twice as often" comparison is a warm-up effect. New pods have a cold cache, so they time out against the replica. The same gap appeared in all five recent rollouts, including a config-only redeploy, and it adds only 10–20 errors. So it doesn't show that v4.18 is faulty. The dashboard counts agree with raw log recounts, so this isn't a counting artefact. I'm fairly confident (about 75%) the week is ordinary variation. I did not establish whether the replica move or partner-sync month-end traffic added anything. Don't roll back, and don't mute the alerting, because that removes the protection that would catch a real problem. Record the week as within the normal band and run the standard check on the following week. If the next week lands above the band, or the burn-rate page fires, open an incident then.
